title: Packaging studio launch pack: pull one strong frame per project from a single continuous studio take, neutralize each to its in-frame grey card so the whole set reads as one grade, cut a sizzle reel and a vertical social cut, and merge a press-ready portfolio board one project per page
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork brief where a small packaging design studio, launching a new website, wanted an 'eye-catching sizzle reel to be used as the hero video on my new site' that is 'fast paced and energetic while showcasing my design work in the best way possible,' built from 'mockups and photographs of packaging projects I have completed.' Laundered to a fictional studio persona ('FOLD & GRAIN', a packaging design studio) — no real company, person, product, marketplace, standard, or trademark is named anywhere, and no craft-software brand names appear in any task-facing field (they are described in generic craft terms). REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the original 'sizzle reel from a folder of loose stills' cannot be produced honestly (there is no still-to-video connector — the tools cannot film, animate stills into motion, or composite motion), and the earlier attempt papered over that by shipping a canned colour preset as 'the grade' across six mismatched photos with no reference to check the match, and by promising motion nothing can synthesise. The corrected design keeps the job the brief actually rewards — turn the studio's own captured material into launch-ready hero deliverables — but routes it to what the connectors genuinely do: the studio shot ONE continuous ~60s 4K studio take, a slow move along a styled shelf of six finished packaging projects with a couple of close passes, and needs (a) the fast sizzle cut and a vertical social cut off that one take, and (b) a PRINTED portfolio board — the leave-behind one-sheet the studio hands to prospective clients — built from the single strongest frame of each project, all graded to one house look. The shelf is lit by mixed sources that drift in colour temperature along its length, and a photographic 18% grey reference card sits in each project's framing under that project's own light, so every pulled still carries a neutral reference and the six frames can be matched to one white point after the fact. Nothing is invented beyond the launch deliverables the brief itself calls for.
one_line_ask: From FOLD & GRAIN's single continuous ~60s 4K studio take, pull the one strongest sharp frame of each of the six packaging projects, neutralize each pulled frame to the 18% grey card that sits in its own framing so the set reads as one continuous house grade (the shelf light drifts, so each frame needs its own white-balance and exposure decision), crop each to the portrait board window without upscaling, cut a fast sizzle reel and a full-length vertical social cut off the same take, vectorize the studio wordmark for the board masthead, then merge the studio's authored one-project-per-page portfolio-board template into a press-ready PDF.
full_brief:
We are FOLD & GRAIN, a small packaging design studio, and we are launching a new website and refreshing the leave-behind one-sheet we hand to prospective clients after a pitch. We are NOT reshooting and we do NOT need a finished, captioned film here — if we want motion-graphic titles later our own editor adds them. What we need from you is the launch pack built off the ONE take we already have.

Here is what you are given: (1) studio_reel_take_4k.mp4 — a single continuous ~60 second 4K (3840x2160) studio take: a slow, steady move along a styled shelf holding six finished packaging projects we have shipped — a kraft tea carton, a frosted-glass cosmetics jar, a matte coffee bag, a printed craft-beer can, a foil perfume box and an illustrated chocolate-bar sleeve — with a couple of slow close passes. Because the shelf is lit by mixed sources and the light changes along its length, the six projects do NOT sit under matching light in the take: some frames come out warm, some cool, some darker, some flat. So we could photograph a reference: a photographic 18% grey card sits in each project's framing, under that project's own light, and stays in shot. (2) portfolio_board_template.indd — the one-project-per-page portfolio-board page we hand-built, with the live placeholder fields and two image slots (the project frame and the masthead). (3) project_list.csv — our six-project run list: the project name, the material, the client sector, a format tag and the approximate position of that project in the take, one row per project. (4) foldgrain_wordmark_flat.png — our flat studio wordmark on transparency, which we want razor-sharp on the board masthead.

What we need back:
- THE SIZZLE (hero video): a fast, energetic short cut off the one take for the top of the homepage, and a full-length vertical (1080x1920) version of the same take for social — same footage, reframed tall, no trimming and no upscaling (the take is 4K, so it has the height for vertical).
- THE PORTFOLIO BOARD (the main print deliverable, and the real craft): a press-ready ~300 DPI PDF of our leave-behind one-sheet, ONE project per page, six pages, that our print vendor runs. For each project on the run list, pull the SINGLE strongest, SHARP frame of that project out of the take (if the position we noted lands on a motion-blurred moment in the move, step to the clean frame beside it — a soft frame prints muddy and we will reject it), grade it, and drop it into the page's project window with its project name, material, sector and format tag bound in from the run list, and our wordmark crisp in the masthead.
- THE GRADE (this is the whole point): the board and the sizzle have to read as ONE studio's work, not six frames grabbed from six different lighting positions. Bring every pulled frame to the SAME house look — a clean, true grade where the neutral grey card in that frame lands truly neutral (no leftover warm or cool cast) at one common white point, and the set shares one exposure feel. Because the shelf light drifts, no two frames start from the same cast or brightness, so getting all six onto that one white point is a per-frame decision — each frame has to be neutralized to its OWN in-frame grey card, and how far and which way to move is yours to judge from that card, frame by frame. A set that is each 'auto-fixed' to look fine on its own will drift apart at the grey cards and we will reject it. Keep the printed package artwork punchy but not blown; neutral, not cast. When you are done, hand back, per frame, the white-balance (temperature / tint) and exposure move you dialed and the final pixel size, so we can confirm the set was matched to one target rather than eyeballed frame by frame.
- PRINT SIZE: each board page drops the frame into a 130 x 173 mm portrait project window, and at press resolution that window needs at least ~1535 x 2044 px of real image. The take is 4K, so a portrait crop taken from the FULL frame just clears that; a frame you graded on a small proxy, or a landscape frame stretched to fill a portrait window, will fall under and print soft — do not enlarge past what the 4K frame actually holds.
- THE WORDMARK: our flat wordmark cleaned to a crisp vector for the board masthead and reusable on future covers.

Keep the sources in our shared cloud folder. Bind the project names, materials, sectors and tags verbatim from the run list — do not rename our projects. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the six frames matched to one white point with the per-frame moves reported; every board frame at least ~1535 x 2044 px so it prints >=300 DPI in the 130 x 173 mm window; the vertical exactly 1080x1920 at the take's full runtime; the wordmark crisp vector on every masthead; and exactly one board page per run-list row.

inputs.name: studio_reel_take_4k.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: CAMERA ORIGINAL (declared at camera scale; no generative video model produces this length/resolution reliably, which is the point — it must be a real capture): a single continuous ~60 second 4K (3840x2160, 16:9, ~24-30fps) hand-held-steady studio take, a slow lateral move along a styled shelf holding six finished, unbranded packaging projects — a kraft loose-leaf tea carton, a frosted-glass cosmetics jar with a metal lid, a matte foil coffee bag with a degassing valve, a printed aluminium craft-beer can, a foil-stamped perfume box, and an illustrated chocolate-bar paper sleeve — arranged left to right, with two slow close push-ins on individual pieces partway through. The shelf is lit by MIXED sources whose colour temperature and brightness DRIFT along its length (a cool window at one end, warm practical/tungsten fill at the other, uneven throw between), so different positions along the shelf sit under visibly different light. A small photographic 18% neutral grey reference card is propped in shot within EACH project's framing, under that project's own light, and remains visible whenever that project is on screen. Real materials, print texture, foil highlights, fold seams and micro-scratches, shallow depth of field, gentle real handheld drift, candid documentary product-video look, NOT glossy CGI, no on-screen text or captions, no real brand names or logos on any object.
inputs.realism_notes: ONE genuine ~60s 4K camera take, declared at camera scale so both downstream needs are honest: (a) frames pulled with video_render_frame are native 3840x2160 stills, so a portrait board crop taken from the FULL frame (max ~1620x2160 for the 130x173mm ~3:4 window) clears the ~1535x2044 print floor without upscaling; (b) video_resize to a same-runtime 9:16 vertical holds >=1080 width from the 4K height (a 9:16 crop of 3840x2160 is ~1215x2160, so 1080x1920 is an honest downscale, never an upscale); and (c) the take is comfortably LONGER than the sizzle target, so video_create_quick_cut has room to shorten it (quick_cut only shortens one longer real take — it cannot lengthen or assemble). THE TRAP / PER-FRAME DIAGNOSIS LIVES HERE: because the shelf light drifts, the six projects are pulled from DIFFERENT casts and exposures and cannot be matched with one blanket correction. Roughly: the kraft tea carton frame is warm and bright; the frosted cosmetics jar cool; the matte coffee bag underexposed with crushed shadow detail; the beer can near-neutral but flat and low-contrast; the foil perfume box warm with a hot foil specular to protect; the chocolate sleeve cool and slightly hazy. The naive path (one global white-balance for all six, or per-frame auto-tone that keys off each frame's own histogram) leaves the warm and cool frames disagreeing at the grey cards and the board reads as a mismatched grab-bag — each frame must instead be neutralized, in its own direction and amount, to the static in-frame 18% grey card that carries that frame's light. The grey card stays in each project's framing so every pulled still carries the reference; it is cropped OUT of the delivered board crops but RETAINED in the card-bearing masters for grade audit. The ~60s runtime is longer than any target derived from it (single-frame stills; a shorter sizzle; a same-length vertical reframe) and the take is a real capture, not an ~8s AI clip.

inputs.name: portfolio_board_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built page-layout data-merge document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A4 portrait (210 x 297 mm) portfolio-board page with 3 mm bleed — ONE project per page. It must contain live data-merge placeholder fields <<ProjectNo>>, <<ProjectName>>, <<Material>>, <<Sector>>, <<FormatTag>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a 130 x 173 mm portrait project frame bound to @Frame (the graded pulled still for that project), and a small masthead lockup frame at the top of the page bound to @Wordmark (the vectorized studio wordmark). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is not available, the wordmark reaches the masthead ONLY as a merge bind through this second image frame — it is not dropped in by hand. The <<ProjectName>> text frame has auto-size 'shrink text to fit' enabled so a long project name binds without going overset. The board furniture (grid rule, caption bar, page ground, footer) is already drawn into the template and is fixed on every page, so the only per-row imagery is the project frame and the masthead wordmark. Built by hand so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT produced by converting a flat PDF to a layout document (that would not bind the merge fields) and NOT a multi-up contact sheet: the data-merge emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd/.idml carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record one-project-per-page board is the correct, connector-doable shape (six rows => a six-page board), never a multi-up contact sheet. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted layout with literal typed text would not bind (convert_pdf_to_indd is a banned merge target). TWO image columns (@Frame, @Wordmark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row — the row's graded board frame AND the shared vectorized wordmark — so the chain-produced wordmark has a real, connector-doable path onto every masthead without any free-form placement (document_merge_data_vector is text-only and could not bind these image columns, which is why the layout merge is used). Column names must exactly match the run-list headers.

inputs.name: project_list.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with headers exactly: ProjectNo,ProjectName,Material,Sector,FormatTag,Position,@Frame,@Wordmark and 6 rows, one per shelf project, in shelf order. ProjectNo is 01..06. ProjectName is the human project name and MUST include at least one deliberately LONG name (e.g. 'Amber Hill Single-Origin Pour-Over Coffee', ~40+ chars) alongside short ones (e.g. 'Leaf & Ash Tea', 'Solene Perfume') so the template's shrink-to-fit is exercised. Material is a short descriptive material note per project (e.g. 'kraft carton', 'frosted glass jar', 'matte foil bag', 'printed aluminium can', 'foil-stamped box', 'illustrated paper sleeve') describing only the substrate — it MUST NOT name any lighting cast, colour temperature, exposure or grade direction. Sector is a short client-sector label ('Beverage', 'Beauty', 'Confectionery', etc.). FormatTag is one of exactly two values: 'Portfolio Board' or 'Web Hero'. Position is an approximate position label of that project in the take ('00:04','00:14','00:22','00:33','00:44','00:54') — a client-supplied label the agent binds and uses to locate the project in the take, NOT a value the agent measures. @Frame holds the agreed prepped board-frame filename for that project (frame_01_final.jpg ... frame_06_final.jpg, in row order) so the merge drops the correct graded frame onto that page. @Wordmark holds 'foldgrain_wordmark.svg' on EVERY row (the same vectorized masthead lockup binds onto every page). Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<ProjectNo>>,<<ProjectName>>,<<Material>>,<<Sector>>,<<FormatTag>> and the two @image-path columns. No column encodes any grade, lighting or treatment direction, and no column encodes the answer via a file-type flag — every row is the same kind of job.
inputs.realism_notes: Six rows => the merge must produce exactly six board pages (page-count = row-count gate). The @Frame column holds the filenames the agent must produce and upload under those exact names, so naming discipline is a real dependency; @Wordmark repeats the single vectorized SVG so the agent-owned masthead lands on every page. Material/Sector/ProjectName/Position are client copy bound verbatim (Position values are the client's run-list labels of where each project sits in the take, not agent measurements, and carry NO cast/exposure hint — the correction direction stays the freelancer's decision read from the in-frame grey card, never a value read off the CSV). The long coffee project name exercises the auto-fit name frame. FormatTag is a descriptive routing label only and does not vary the per-frame treatment (all six frames get the same pull->neutralize->crop job — there is no hidden triage encoded in a column or a file extension).

inputs.name: foldgrain_wordmark_flat.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Flat minimalist studio wordmark on a TRANSPARENT background: the words 'FOLD & GRAIN' set in a clean high-contrast sans, a small folded-corner glyph beside it, solid single-colour (near-black ink) glyphs, crisp clean hard edges, high contrast, centred with a generous transparent margin all around, no gradients, no photographic texture, no sheen, exported slightly oversized and off-centre, 2400x700 PNG with alpha.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat, hard-edged, single-colour text art on transparent alpha so image_vectorize produces clean closed SVG paths after prep-before-trace (crop-to-bounds to strip the generous transparent margin, then a crisp contrast pass so the edges separate hard). Text-bearing wordmark -> gemini-3-pro-image for legible letterforms. It is a SUPPLIED asset only cleaned and vectorized, never a from-scratch designed letterform. On a light masthead the traced mark's closed counters read correctly; no dark-ground knockout of enclosed counters is claimed.

outputs.name: FoldGrain_Launch_PortfolioBoard_x6.pdf
outputs.spec: THE PRIMARY, AGENT-OWNED PRINT DELIVERABLE. A press-ready ~300 DPI A4 portrait (210 x 297 mm) + 3 mm bleed portfolio board, ONE project per page, SIX pages (page-count = run-list row-count = 6), exported from the one-file-per-row layout data-merge. Each page binds its ProjectNo/ProjectName/Material/Sector/FormatTag verbatim from the run list, drops that project's grey-card-neutralized, house-graded board frame into the 130 x 173 mm portrait project window (>=1535 x 2044 px so it prints >=300 DPI), and drops the vectorized wordmark into the masthead lockup. The board reads as one continuous grade across all six pages. The 'hero' is simply page one of the merged board (no per-record named export). Its distinctive quality — the matched grade, the single-frame selection per project, the crisp masthead — is the agent's, not a template default. [C/T]

outputs.name: board_frame_masters_cardbearing_x6
outputs.spec: Six grey-card-neutralized full-frame masters (native ~3840x2160), one per pulled project, each with its in-frame 18% grey card driven to a clean neutral and the whole set matched to one shared white point and exposure feel while the printed artwork stays true (punchy, not blown; neutral, not cast). The grey card is RETAINED in frame in these masters — this is the grade-audit artifact the grader checks neutrality on (the card is cropped out of the board frames, so neutrality is graded HERE, on the retained card-bearing masters, not on the delivered board). Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance (temperature/tint) and exposure move AND the final pixel dimensions of each frame. [C]

outputs.name: board_frames_x6
outputs.spec: Six portrait board crops (frame_01_final.jpg ... frame_06_final.jpg), each cropped from the FULL-resolution card-bearing master to the 130 x 173 mm (~3:4) project-window ratio with the grey card cropped OUT, held at >=1535 x 2044 px (target ~1620 x 2160, the maximum a portrait crop of the 4K frame holds) so each prints >=300 DPI in the window. These are the @Frame assets the merge resolves per row; the card-exclusion is checked here separately from the neutrality check on the masters. [C]

outputs.name: foldgrain_sizzle_16x9.mp4
outputs.spec: A fast, short sizzle cut for the homepage hero, produced by shortening the single ~60s 4K take with video_create_quick_cut (the tool selects the cut; output duration < source). Honours the brief's 'fast paced and energetic' hero-video ask. Frame-accurate motion-graphic titles, if wanted, are the studio's own finish, not claimed here. [A]

outputs.name: foldgrain_sizzle_9x16.mp4
outputs.spec: A full-length 9:16 vertical (1080x1920) reframe of the whole ~60s 4K take for the vertical social slot — SAME runtime as the source (subject-aware reframe only, no trim), produced by video_resize [A]. The 4K master's height carries a 9:16 crop of ~1215x2160, so 1080x1920 is an honest downscale, never an upscale. [A]

outputs.name: foldgrain_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: The flat studio wordmark cleaned and vectorized to a crisp SVG (prep-before-trace: crop-to-bounds then a crisp contrast pass then trace), razor-sharp at any size, bound into every board masthead via the @Wordmark column and reusable on future covers. [C]

outputs.name: grade_report.txt
outputs.spec: A plain parameter sheet the agent authors and returns (NOT the primary output; the board PDF is): for each of the six pulled projects, the white-balance temperature and tint and the exposure move that were applied, plus the final pixel size of each board frame, plus the single common house white point all six were matched to. This makes 'the set is matched to one target' checkable — the corrections must be non-identical across the warm and cool frames. It is an applied-settings log, never a measured/recovered pixel readout. [C]

The agent chooses the exact frame — if the noted position lands on a motion-blurred moment in the move, step to the clean adjacent frame (a soft frame prints muddy on the board). Goal only: get the cleanest single frame of this project. [A].

The correction each frame needs is its own — judge direction and amount from this frame's card, not from a global setting. Shorten the single ~60s 4K take into a fast, energetic homepage sizzle cut (output duration < source; the tool selects the cut). quick_cut only SHORTENS one longer real take — it does not lengthen or assemble multiple clips, and the ~60s source is comfortably longer than the sizzle target. Initialize a block upload of the flat studio wordmark foldgrain_wordmark_flat.png (media_type image/png, transparent alpha) so it can be prepped and vectorized for the board masthead. Plumbing.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: frame_01_final, frame_02_final, frame_03_final, frame_04_final, frame_05_final, frame_06_final, foldgrain_wordmark.svg

Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the run list's @Frame / @Wordmark columns resolve to for each board page.

One-file-per-row layout data-merge: bind each of the six run-list rows (ProjectNo/ProjectName/Material/Sector/FormatTag) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and drop that row's graded board frame into the @Frame window AND the vectorized wordmark into the @Wordmark masthead — producing EXACTLY ONE board page per row (six pages); the auto-fit frame shrinks the long coffee project name. [T] requires the hand-authored template. A converted-PDF template or a multi-up contact sheet would not bind / cannot be produced; document_merge_data_vector is text-only and could not bind the two image columns.

Export the merged single-record pages to a press-ready ~300 DPI A4 + 3 mm bleed PDF with crop marks, one project per page. The whole merged document exports as one file (no per-record named export; the hero is simply page one). Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 6; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed. FINAL primary deliverable.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining anchored on the one client take. VIDEO SPINE: the 4K take is uploaded (1) and finalized (2 -> take_asset); video_metadata (3) reads its duration/format so the six run-list positions sample across the real ~60s. Six video_render_frame pulls (4-9) each pull a DIFFERENT project at a DIFFERENT run-list Position from take_asset (the creative selection the agent owns — which project, which sharp frame), yielding native 3840x2160 stills frame_01_raw..frame_06_raw. Each raw frame drives its own two-step grade sub-chain: an image_apply_adjustments neutralization to the in-frame 18% grey card (adaptive per frame — the correction is judged from each frame's own card because the shelf light drifts) whose output is the RETAINED card-bearing master (10,12,14,16,18,20), followed by an image_crop_and_resize (11,13,15,17,19,21) that crops the grey card OUT and reframes on the package to the 3:4 board window from the FULL master at >=1535x2044 px. Every neutralization is driven to that frame's own grey card so all six converge on one shared white point. The same take feeds two independent video deliverables: video_create_quick_cut (22) shortens it into the homepage sizzle, and video_resize (23) reframes it to the same-runtime 1080x1920 vertical. WORDMARK BRANCH: upload-init (24) -> finalize (25 -> wordmark_asset) -> crop_to_bounds (26) -> crisp adjustments (27) -> image_vectorize (28 -> foldgrain_wordmark.svg). CONVERGENCE: the six board frames and the vectorized wordmark fan into the merge upload session (29) -> finalize (30 -> merge_asset_urns) -> document_merge_data_layout (31), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the run-list CSV and emits one board page per row resolving BOTH @Frame and @Wordmark; the merged set exports to the per-project press PDF (32).
